react_result.final_narrative_text: Metabolomics analysis of 10 differentially abundant metabolites revealed a dominant and strongly corroborated enrichment of the tryptophan metabolism pathway across three independent over-representation analyses. L-Tryptophan (C00078) — the canonical entry-point substrate — was recovered by both RaMP-DB (multi-DB ORA) and MetaboAnalystR (KEGG-specific PSEA) alongside six downstream metabolites: tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde (indol-3-ylacetaldehyde), and 3-aminopropanal. This 6-metabolite hit set yields an FDR of 3.4×10⁻¹⁵ in RaMP (KEGG:map00380) and a raw p-value of 5.4×10⁻⁹ in MetaboAnalystR (KEGG:hsa00380), placing tryptophan metabolism as the unequivocal top-ranked pathway in both independent methods. WikiPathways concordance is also seen (WP:WP465). Secondary pathway hits include Reactome Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (FDR 3.6×10⁻⁸) and Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (FDR 1.3×10⁻⁸), consistent with tryptophan serving as the shared precursor for the serotonergic and kynurenine branches. 4-Hydroxy-L-glutamic acid and molybdenum were not recovered in top pathways, suggesting peripheral involvement. InChIKey reconciliation across 9 metabolites confirmed zero structural conflicts. The biological story is one of systemic tryptophan pathway activation: L-tryptophan is the hub, with differential metabolites spanning its major downstream arms — the serotonergic/melatonergic branch (serotonin → melatonin), the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid), and the decarboxylated/deaminated branch (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-aminopropanal). The treatment condition most plausibly shifts tryptophan flux away from or between these branches, dysregulating neuroactive amine synthesis and, indirectly, NAD+ biosynthesis via the kynurenine route.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three over-representation analyses (RaMP-DB multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR PSEA, and mummichog m/z-directed activity) converged on a single dominant pathway: Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380 / hsa00380). RaMP-DB reported FDR = 3.44e-15 with fold enrichment 751; MetaboAnalystR reported raw p = 5.41e-09 with 6 metabolites recovered (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine); mummichog reported p = 0.0026 with 13 of 14 pathway members detected from the input list, including the same six plus the L/D-tryptophan pair and 3-aminopropanal. The three tools show concordant compound rosters confirming that L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), and melatonin (KEGG:C01598) are the primary signal compounds driving the enrichment. RaMP-DB further recovered Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) at FDR 3.59e-08 and Biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550) at FDR 3.98e-08, both corroborating the serotonergic branch as a key affected subsystem. Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR 6.90e-08) confirms that the kynurenine arm is also perturbed, as evidenced by the presence of 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632) in the hit list. Vitamin A (retinol) metabolism (MUMM:vitamin_a_retinol_metabolism, rank 4, p = 0.048) was flagged only by mummichog and does not replicate in the ORA tools, indicating it is likely a lower-confidence secondary signal. 3-Aminopropanal (KEGG:C05665) was recovered in the Histidine metabolism cluster by mummichog only; it is a shared intermediate and its cross-pathway presence is biologically consistent.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Metabolomics analysis of 10 differentially abundant metabolites revealed a dominant and strongly corroborated enrichment of the tryptophan metabolism pathway across three independent over-representation analyses. L-Tryptophan (C00078) — the canonical entry-point substrate — was recovered by both RaMP-DB (multi-DB ORA) and MetaboAnalystR (KEGG-specific PSEA) alongside six downstream metabolites: tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde (indol-3-ylacetaldehyde), and 3-aminopropanal. This 6-metabolite hit set yields an FDR of 3.4×10⁻¹⁵ in RaMP (KEGG:map00380) and a raw p-value of 5.4×10⁻⁹ in MetaboAnalystR (KEGG:hsa00380), placing tryptophan metabolism as the unequivocal top-ranked pathway in both independent methods. WikiPathways concordance is also seen (WP:WP465). Secondary pathway hits include Reactome Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (FDR 3.6×10⁻⁸) and Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (FDR 1.3×10⁻⁸), consistent with tryptophan serving as the shared precursor for the serotonergic and kynurenine branches. 4-Hydroxy-L-glutamic acid and molybdenum were not recovered in top pathways, suggesting peripheral involvement. InChIKey reconciliation across 9 metabolites confirmed zero structural conflicts. The biological story is one of systemic tryptophan pathway activation: L-tryptophan is the hub, with differential metabolites spanning its major downstream arms — the serotonergic/melatonergic branch (serotonin → melatonin), the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid), and the decarboxylated/deaminated branch (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-aminopropanal). The treatment condition most plausibly shifts tryptophan flux away from or between these branches, dysregulating neuroactive amine synthesis and, indirectly, NAD+ biosynthesis via the kynurenine route.
